derivations.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$ and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate. This $a$ is not a bank index.

Replacing $j_i$ by $j_i+t_i$ changes the exponent by $-\pi i s_i\frac{(j_i+t_i)^2-j_i^2}{t_i}=-\pi i s_i(2j_i+t_i)$, which is an integral multiple of $2\pi i$ because $t_i$ is even, so $a$ has period $t_i$ in coordinate $i$.

In the right side, the coefficient of $u_{\boldsymbol k}$ at position $\boldsymbol j$ is $\frac1T\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}$. Using $(j_i-k_i)^2=j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2$, the exponent of this product is $\sum_i\frac{\pi i s_i}{t_i}\bigl(j_i^2-(j_i^2-2j_ik_i+k_i^2)+k_i^2\bigr)$, so the coefficient is $\frac1T\overline a_{\boldsymbol j}a_{\boldsymbol j-\boldsymbol k}\overline a_{\boldsymbol k}=\frac1T\exp(2\pi i\sum_is_ij_ik_i/t_i)$.
This is precisely the coefficient of $QF_{\boldsymbol t}$ above, because $Q$ reads frequency $(-s_ij_i)_i$ from the negative-sign transform.

symbols.name: position
symbols.meaning: A position in an array, one index per axis.
symbols.quote: Arrays have $d$ axes and are indexed by positions $\boldsymbol j=(j_1,\dots,j_d)$.

symbols.name: axis lengths
symbols.meaning: The tuple of the even axis lengths.
symbols.quote: The tuple $\boldsymbol t=(t_1,\dots,t_d)$ lists the axis lengths, each even,

symbols.name: coprime multiplier
symbols.meaning: An integer coprime to the axis length t_i.
symbols.quote: and $s_i$ is an integer coprime to $t_i$.

symbols.name: input position
symbols.meaning: An input position of the transform.
symbols.quote: where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

symbols.name: frequency
symbols.meaning: The frequency labelling an output entry.
symbols.quote: where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

symbols.name: normalized transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform with axis lengths t.
symbols.quote: The normalized transform $F_{\boldsymbol t}$ is given by $(F_{\boldsymbol t}u)_{\boldsymbol f}=\frac1T\sum_{\boldsymbol k}u_{\boldsymbol k}\exp(-2\pi i\sum_i k_if_i/t_i)$, where $\boldsymbol k$ runs over input positions and $\boldsymbol f=(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ is the frequency labelling an output entry.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of the output that puts at position j the entry of frequency (-s_i j_i)_i.
symbols.quote: Gaussian resampling leaves a target permutation $Q$, a reordering of the output of a power-of-two transform; the identity absorbs $Q$ into a convolution, so it is never executed as a sort

symbols.name: chirp
symbols.meaning: The chirp, a phase quadratic in the position.
symbols.quote: Define the chirp $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d s_ij_i^2/t_i\right)$ and let $\overline a$ be its complex conjugate. This $a$ is not a bank index.

relations.quote: The Bluestein chirp identity rewrites a permuted [Discrete Fourier transform](dft.md) as a pointwise chirp phase, a cyclic convolution, and another chirp phase.
The permuted transform is thus reduced to one [Cyclic convolution](convolution.md) of length $T$ between two pointwise phase multiplications.
